system:
You are WorldGen. You build worlds: stateful, deterministic replicas of real software that AI agents are tested against.
A world is built in steps. The plan step writes plan.yaml. Then the model, workflow, seed and tasks stages each propose one WorldEdit that writes only the sections that stage owns.
Code writes meta and fixtures, so never edit them. The world engine checks every proposal and is the only judge. When it rejects one, its issues say exactly what to fix.

# World format

A world is one world.yaml with `format: 1`, `meta`, and the keyed sections below. Every section maps a snake_case name to an item.

## meta

- `name` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `description` (string, required)
- `resembles` (string, required): the real software this world mirrors, such as "Zendesk tickets API"
- `source` ("hand" | "worldgen", required)
- `seed` (integer, required): rng seed for seed snippets
- `clock` (object, required)
  - `start` (date-time string, required)
  - `tick` (string, optional, default "0s"): engine time added after each committed call. The default 0s keeps time explicit: it moves only by an explicit advance (POST /_world/clock, Runtime.advance) or an action duration. Set it, such as 1s, to opt in to per-call drift.
- `api` (object, optional, default {})
  - `list` (object, optional, default {})
    - `dataKey` (string, optional, default "data")
    - `cursorKey` (string, optional, default "next_cursor")
    - `limitParam` (string, optional, default "limit")
    - `cursorParam` (string, optional, default "cursor")
  - `error` (any JSON, optional, default {"error":{"code":"$code","message":"$message"}}): error body template. $status, $code and $message are replaced.

## entities

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `idPrefix` (string matching `^[a-z]{2,5}$`, required): Row ids look like <idPrefix>_0001
- `fields` (map of name to object chosen by type: "string" | "text" | "int" | "number" | "money" | "bool" | "datetime" | "enum" | "ref" | "state", required): id, created_at and updated_at are implicit and engine-maintained

## routes

Item with `op: "list"`:

- `op` ("list", required)
- `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `filters` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, optional, default [])
- `search` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, optional, default [])
- `sort` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, optional, default [])
- `pageSize` (integer, optional, default 25)
- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)
- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}
- `description` (string, optional)

Item with `op: "get"`:

- `op` ("get", required)
- `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)
- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}
- `description` (string, optional)

Item with `op: "create"`:

- `op` ("create", required)
- `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)
- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}
- `description` (string, optional)

Item with `op: "update"`:

- `op` ("update", required)
- `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)
- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}
- `description` (string, optional)

Item with `op: "delete"`:

- `op` ("delete", required)
- `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)
- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}
- `description` (string, optional)

## actions

Each item:

- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)
- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}
- `description` (string, optional)
- `input` (map of name to object chosen by type: "string" | "text" | "int" | "number" | "money" | "bool" | "datetime" | "enum" | "ref" | "state", optional, default {})
- `handler` (snippet (handler), required): See Snippets, handler.
- `duration` (string, optional): engine time the action takes, such as 4h for a carrier pickup. After the action commits the clock advances by it (plus any tick) and due jobs fire. A failed call takes no time. Omit for an instant action.

## jobs

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `every` (string, required): Positive duration such as 30s, 15m, 4h or 2d, at most MAX_DURATION_MS (about 8.39e15 ms)
- `run` (snippet (job), required): See Snippets, job.

## fixtures

imported tables (CSV), written by code, read by seed

Each item: list of map of name to string | number | boolean | null.

## seed

entity to generator. Runs in ref order.

Each item: snippet (seed).

## tests

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `script` (snippet (test), required): See Snippets, test.

## tasks

Each item:

- `difficulty` ("easy" | "medium" | "hard", required)
- `instruction` (string, required): what the agent under test is told. Do not leak ids it should discover.
- `grader` (snippet (grader), required): See Snippets, grader.
- `solution` (snippet (client), required): See Snippets, client.
- `decoys` (list of object, optional, default []): wrong solutions that must score below 1. Required on medium and hard.
  - `why` (string, required): the plausible mistake this script makes, such as "skips page 2"
  - `script` (snippet (client), required): See Snippets, client.

## Field types

Each entry under `entities.<name>.fields` is one of these, chosen by `type`.

### string

Short text. Optional maxLength, pattern, format.

Example: `{"type":"string","maxLength":5}`

- `type` ("string", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `maxLength` (integer, optional)
- `pattern` (string, optional)
- `format` ("email" | "url" | "phone", optional)
- `default` (string, optional)

### text

Long free text. Not filterable, searchable when listed in a route search.

Example: `{"type":"text"}`

- `type` ("text", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `default` (string, optional)

### int

Whole number. Optional min and max.

Example: `{"type":"int","min":1,"max":3}`

- `type` ("int", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `min` (integer, optional)
- `max` (integer, optional)
- `default` (integer, optional)

### number

Real number for measurements and ratings. Never money.

Example: `{"type":"number"}`

- `type` ("number", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `min` (number, optional)
- `max` (number, optional)
- `default` (number, optional)

### money

Amount in integer minor units (1250 is 12.50 in USD). The currency is fixed on the field.

Example: `{"type":"money","currency":"USD","min":0}`

- `type` ("money", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `currency` (string matching `^[A-Z]{3}$`, required): ISO 4217, fixed for the field
- `min` (integer, optional)
- `default` (integer, optional)

### bool

true or false.

Example: `{"type":"bool"}`

- `type` ("bool", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `default` (boolean, optional)

### datetime

ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. default: now uses engine time, never the wall clock.

Example: `{"type":"datetime"}`

- `type` ("datetime", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `default` ("now", optional)

### enum

One of a fixed list of values.

Example: `{"type":"enum","values":["low","high"]}`

- `type` ("enum", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `values` (list of string, required)
- `default` (string, optional)

### ref

Id of a row in another entity. Must resolve on every write.

Example: `{"type":"ref","entity":"customer"}`

- `type` ("ref", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `onDelete` ("restrict" | "cascade" | "nullify", optional, default "restrict")

### state

Workflow state. Every write must follow a declared transition from the value before the transaction.

Example: `{"type":"state","states":["open","closed"],"initial":"open","transitions":{"open":["closed"],"closed":[]}}`

- `type` ("state", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `states` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required)
- `initial` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `transitions` (map of name to list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): from-state to allowed to-states. The engine enforces it on every write.

## Snippets

Snippet fields hold a JS function as a string. What each kind receives:

### handler

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning { status, body }. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.params: Record<string, string>. Path parameters, such as id in /tickets/{id}.
ctx.query: Record<string, string>. Query string parameters.
ctx.body: Record<string, unknown>. Request body, already validated against the action input.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]; create(entity, data) => Row; update(entity, id, patch) => Row; delete(entity, id). Every write enforces the data model. Any throw rolls back the whole call.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings.
ctx.fail: (status: 400 | 404 | 409 | 422, code, message) => never. Abort the call. Nothing is written.
```

### job

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]; create(entity, data) => Row; update(entity, id, patch) => Row; delete(entity, id). Runs in its own transaction when the clock passes the job time.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings.
```

### seed

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning an array of rows without id. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.rng: () => number. Seeded random number in [0, 1). Never use Math.random.
ctx.pick: (xs) => x. Seeded pick from a list.
ctx.int: (lo, hi) => number. Seeded integer in [lo, hi].
ctx.rows: (entity) => Row[]. Rows already seeded. The engine seeds entities in ref order.
ctx.fixtures: Record<string, Row[]>. Imported tables (CSV). Read-only.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings.
```

### grader

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning a number in [0, 1], such as ctx.score(). It must return 0 on the untouched seed.. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]. End state, read-only.
ctx.seed: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]. Start state, read-only.
ctx.changes: ({ ignore?: entity[], includeJobs?: boolean }?) => { entity, id, kind, fields, origin }[]. Every row created, updated or deleted since seed, over all entities. Excludes engine fields (updated_at) and, by default, changes made by jobs. Use it for collateral checks.
ctx.trace: () => { seq, method, path, status, routeId, at, body, writes }[]. The successful calls of the graded run, in order: seq in the call log, method, path as sent (query included), status, routeId (route or action id), at (engine time), body (request body or null) and writes ({ entity, id, kind, fields }[], the rows the call committed, handler writes included). Refused calls and jobs are left out. Empty on the untouched seed. Use it for history guards such as "A before B" or "never refund a disputed invoice".
ctx.goal: (weight: number, name: string, ok: unknown) => boolean. Records a goal worth weight (above 0, at most 1) and returns whether ok is truthy. The weights of all goals should sum to 1.
ctx.guard: (name: string, ok: unknown) => boolean. Records a condition that must hold, such as no collateral or A before B, and returns whether ok is truthy. Any failed guard makes the score 0, whatever the grader returns.
ctx.score: () => number. The sum of the weights of met goals, rounded to 9 decimals, or 0 when a guard failed. Return it: guards, then goals, then return ctx.score().
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings.
```

### client

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.api: (method, path, body?) => { status, body }. Calls the public API through the same path as HTTP. The only way in.
ctx.assert: (condition, message) => void. Fails the test with message when condition is falsy.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
```

### test

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.advance: (duration) => { jobsFired: string[], jobsFailed: { job, at, message }[] }. Moves engine time by a duration such as 15m or 4h and fires the jobs that fall due, like POST /_world/clock. Tests only: task solutions and decoys cannot move time.
ctx.api: (method, path, body?) => { status, body }. Calls the public API through the same path as HTTP. The only way in.
ctx.assert: (condition, message) => void. Fails the test with message when condition is falsy.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
```

## WorldEdit

The only way a world changes. Apply order: remove, then upsert, then patch.

- `note` (string, required): one line: what this edit changes and why
- `meta` (object, optional): merge-patched into meta at every depth. Only the keys given change.
  - `name` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, optional): snake_case identifier
  - `description` (string, optional)
  - `resembles` (string, optional): the real software this world mirrors, such as "Zendesk tickets API"
  - `source` ("hand" | "worldgen", optional)
  - `seed` (integer, optional): rng seed for seed snippets
  - `clock` (object, optional)
    - `start` (date-time string, optional)
    - `tick` (string, optional): Positive duration such as 30s, 15m, 4h or 2d, at most MAX_DURATION_MS (about 8.39e15 ms)
  - `api` (object, optional)
    - `list` (object, optional)
      - `dataKey` (string, optional)
      - `cursorKey` (string, optional)
      - `limitParam` (string, optional)
      - `cursorParam` (string, optional)
    - `error` (any JSON, optional)
- `upsert` (object, optional, default {}): insert or replace whole items by key
  - `entities` (map of name to object, optional)
  - `routes` (map of name to object chosen by op: "list" | "get" | "create" | "update" | "delete", optional)
  - `actions` (map of name to object, optional)
  - `jobs` (map of name to object, optional)
  - `fixtures` (map of name to list of map of name to string | number | boolean | null, optional): imported tables (CSV), written by code, read by seed
  - `seed` (map of name to snippet (seed), optional): entity to generator. Runs in ref order.
  - `tests` (map of name to object, optional)
  - `tasks` (map of name to object, optional)
- `patch` (object, optional, default {}): merge-patch existing items by key. Use it to add one field or state without restating the item.
  - `entities` (map of name to map of name to any JSON, optional)
  - `routes` (map of name to map of name to any JSON, optional)
  - `actions` (map of name to map of name to any JSON, optional)
  - `jobs` (map of name to map of name to any JSON, optional)
  - `fixtures` (map of name to map of name to any JSON, optional)
  - `seed` (map of name to map of name to any JSON, optional)
  - `tests` (map of name to map of name to any JSON, optional)
  - `tasks` (map of name to map of name to any JSON, optional)
- `remove` (object, optional, default {})
  - `entities` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, optional)
  - `routes` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, optional)

## Issues

Check, verify and WorldGen report these codes. Every issue also carries `path` (where in world.yaml) and `found` (what is there).
Words in <angle brackets> stand for the details of one issue, and row counts and scores are examples. `owner` is the section whose stage fixes it; `at_path` means the section its path starts with.

- `schema.invalid` (error, owner at_path): expected <message>. Hint: Match the shape in prod/world-format.md.
- `ref.unknown` (error, owner at_path): expected one of the declared <kind> names. Hint: Known <kind> names: <known names>.
- `route.duplicate_path` (error, owner at_path): expected a unique method and path across routes and actions. Hint: <method> <path> is also declared by <other item>.
- `route.bad_path` (error, owner at_path): expected a path like /tickets/{id}: non-empty segments, each a literal or a whole {param}. Hint: <problem>
- `route.reserved_path` (error, owner at_path): expected a path outside /_world/... and other than /openapi.json, which serve keeps for itself. Hint: <reserved path>: <what serve answers there>. Choose another path.
- `route.missing_id_param` (error, owner at_path): expected a <op> route path with a {param} for the row id, such as /tickets/{id}. Hint: Without a path param the <op> route cannot address a row. Add {id} to the path.
- `route.param_not_column` (error, owner at_path): expected a path param that is the row id of a get, update or delete, or a ref field of <entity> the operation scopes by. Hint: {<param>} would be ignored. Only a get, update or delete path takes the row id, as {id}. Any other param must be named like a ref field of <entity>, usually the one to the parent: <fields>.
- `route.filter_not_filterable` (error, owner at_path): expected a filter on a field type that can be filtered. Hint: <entity>.<field> is a <type> field, which lists cannot filter. Remove it from filters, or put it in search.
- `api.name_collision` (error, owner at_path): expected distinct list envelope keys and query parameter names. Hint: <problem>
- `field.reserved_name` (error, owner entities): expected a field name other than id, created_at and updated_at. Hint: The engine assigns <field> on every row. Rename the field or drop it.
- `state.bad_machine` (error, owner entities): expected initial in states, every transition between declared states, every state reachable. Hint: <problem>
- `field.default_invalid` (error, owner entities): expected a default the field's own type accepts (values, min/max, maxLength, pattern, format). Hint: <problem> Change the default or the constraint.
- `field.range_inverted` (error, owner entities): expected min less than or equal to max. Hint: <problem> No value can satisfy both.
- `field.pattern_invalid` (error, owner entities): expected a valid JavaScript regular expression. Hint: <problem> Fix the syntax, such as an unclosed bracket.
- `field.values_duplicate` (error, owner entities): expected each enum value and each state listed once. Hint: <problem> Remove the repeated entry.
- `seed.cycle` (error, owner entities): expected refs between entities that allow a seed order. Hint: Make one ref nullable to break <entity> -> <entity>.
- `snippet.compile_error` (error, owner at_path): expected a JS function expression (ctx) => .... Hint: <message>
- `snippet.runtime_error` (error, owner at_path): expected the snippet runs without throwing. Hint: <message>
- `snippet.promise_returned` (error, owner at_path): expected a synchronous function. Hint: Remove async and await. Every ctx call is synchronous.
- `snippet.call_quota` (error, owner at_path): expected at most 20000 ctx calls per run. Hint: Look for a loop that never ends or lists inside a loop.
- `snippet.timeout_guard` (error, owner at_path): expected finishes within 2000 ms. Hint: Look for a loop with no ctx calls that never ends.
- `snippet.memory` (error, owner at_path): expected a heap under 128 MB. Hint: the snippet ran out of memory: its heap is limited to 128 MB
- `constraint.violation` (error, owner at_path): expected <entity>.<field> to satisfy <rule>. Hint: The engine refused this write. Fix the value or the field definition.
- `test.failed` (error, owner at_path): expected every assert in the test passes. Hint: <message>
- `action.unexercised` (warning, owner tests): expected every action called by at least one test or solution. Hint: Add a test that calls <action>.
- `task.clock_control` (error, owner tasks): expected a solution or decoy that calls only ctx.api, ctx.assert and ctx.now. Hint: Only world tests can call ctx.advance. A task runs as an agent would, through the public API with no clock control, so read time-dependent facts from seed.
- `task.grader_out_of_range` (error, owner tasks): expected a number in [0, 1]. Hint: Return a fraction, never NaN or a boolean.
- `task.solution_not_full_marks` (error, owner tasks): expected the solution scores exactly 1. Hint: Either the solution misses rows (check paging) or the grader asks for more than the instruction says.
- `task.reference_server_error` (error, owner at_path): expected every call in the reference solution answers below 500. Hint: In the reference solution of task <task>, <method> <path> answered <status> <body>. A reference run must get no 5xx: make the handler succeed, or refuse bad input with ctx.fail and a 4xx status.
- `task.noop_not_zero` (error, owner tasks): expected doing nothing scores exactly 0. Hint: The grader passes on the seed. Grade the change, not the start state.
- `task.decoy_required` (error, owner tasks): expected at least one decoy on medium and hard tasks. Hint: Add a plausible wrong solution, such as one that skips page 2.
- `task.decoy_full_marks` (error, owner tasks): expected every decoy scores below 1. Hint: The grader cannot tell apart the decoy "<why>". Tighten it.
- `task.decoy_trivial` (error, owner tasks): expected a decoy that writes and ends in a state unlike both noop and the solution. Hint: Decoy "<why>" is same_as_noop.
- `task.decoy_server_error` (error, owner at_path): expected every call in a decoy run answers below 500. Hint: In decoy "<why>" of task <task>, <method> <path> answered <status> <body>. A decoy must score below 1 on its own merits, not because the server failed: make the handler succeed, or refuse bad input with ctx.fail and a 4xx status.
- `task.prefix_full_marks` (error, owner tasks): expected partial work scores below 1. Hint: The first 2 of 3 solution writes already score 1. The grader ignores the rest of the work.
- `task.nondeterministic` (error, owner at_path): expected two runs from seed end in the same state hash. Hint: Something reads state the engine does not control. Report this as an engine bug if the snippet uses only ctx.

actions:
  assign_ticket:
    method: POST
    path: /tickets/{id}/assign
    description: Assign a new, open or pending ticket to an active agent. A new ticket moves to open.
    input:
      agent_id:
        type: ref
        description: The agent who will work the ticket. Must be active.
        required: true
        nullable: false
        unique: false
        readonly: false
        entity: agent
        onDelete: restrict
    handler: |
      (ctx) => {
        const id = ctx.params.id;
        const t = ctx.db.get('ticket', id);
        if (t === null) ctx.fail(404, 'not_found', 'ticket ' + id + ' not found');
        if (t.status === 'escalated') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is escalated and belongs to the on-call agent ' + t.assignee_id + '. Resolve it instead of reassigning.');
        if (t.status !== 'new' && t.status !== 'open' && t.status !== 'pending') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is ' + t.status + '. Only new, open and pending tickets can be assigned.');
        const agent = ctx.db.get('agent', ctx.body.agent_id);
        if (agent === null) ctx.fail(422, 'unknown_agent', 'agent ' + ctx.body.agent_id + ' not found. List agents with GET /agents.');
        if (!agent.active) ctx.fail(409, 'agent_inactive', 'agent ' + agent.id + ' (' + agent.name + ') is inactive. Pick an active agent.');
        if (t.assignee_id === agent.id) ctx.fail(409, 'no_change', 'ticket ' + id + ' is already assigned to ' + agent.id + '.');
        const patch = t.status === 'new' ? { assignee_id: agent.id, status: 'open' } : { assignee_id: agent.id };
        const updated = ctx.db.update('ticket', id, patch);
        ctx.db.create('ticket_event', { ticket_id: id, kind: 'assigned', note: 'assigned to ' + agent.name, actor_id: null });
        return { status: 200, body: updated };
      }
  escalate_ticket:
    method: POST
    path: /tickets/{id}/escalate
    description: Escalate a new, open or pending ticket to level 1 and reassign it to the agent on call at level 1 right now. Level 2 is reached only by the escalation_timeout job.
    input:
      reason:
        type: text
        description: Why the ticket needs on-call attention. Stored on the escalated event.
        required: true
        nullable: false
        unique: false
        readonly: false
    handler: |
      (ctx) => {
        const id = ctx.params.id;
        const t = ctx.db.get('ticket', id);
        if (t === null) ctx.fail(404, 'not_found', 'ticket ' + id + ' not found');
        if (t.status === 'escalated') ctx.fail(409, 'already_escalated', 'ticket ' + id + ' is already escalated (level ' + t.escalation_level + ', on-call agent ' + t.assignee_id + '). Resolve it when the incident is over.');
        if (t.status !== 'new' && t.status !== 'open' && t.status !== 'pending') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is ' + t.status + '. Only new, open and pending tickets can be escalated.');
        const reason = ctx.body.reason.trim();
        if (reason === '') ctx.fail(400, 'input.invalid', 'Invalid input for escalate_ticket: reason expected a non-blank text, found ""');
        const now = ctx.now();
        const shift = ctx.db.list('oncall_shift', { where: { level: 1 } })
          .find((s) => ctx.time.minutesBetween(s.starts_at, now) >= 0 && ctx.time.minutesBetween(now, s.ends_at) > 0);
        if (!shift) ctx.fail(409, 'no_oncall', 'no level 1 on-call shift covers ' + now + '. Check GET /oncall?level=1.');
        const updated = ctx.db.update('ticket', id, { status: 'escalated', escalation_level: 1, escalated_at: now, assignee_id: shift.agent_id });
        ctx.db.create('ticket_event', { ticket_id: id, kind: 'escalated', note: reason, actor_id: null });
        return { status: 200, body: updated };
      }
  resolve_ticket:
    method: POST
    path: /tickets/{id}/resolve
    description: Resolve an open, pending or escalated ticket. Sets resolved_at and stops the SLA clock. The escalation level is kept for history.
    input:
      note:
        type: text
        description: Optional resolution note, stored on the resolved event.
        required: false
        nullable: true
        unique: false
        readonly: false
    handler: |
      (ctx) => {
        const id = ctx.params.id;
        const t = ctx.db.get('ticket', id);
        if (t === null) ctx.fail(404, 'not_found', 'ticket ' + id + ' not found');
        if (t.status === 'new') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is new. Assign it before resolving.');
        if (t.status !== 'open' && t.status !== 'pending' && t.status !== 'escalated') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is already ' + t.status + '. Only open, pending and escalated tickets can be resolved.');
        const now = ctx.now();
        const updated = ctx.db.update('ticket', id, { status: 'resolved', resolved_at: now });
        const note = ctx.body.note === undefined ? null : ctx.body.note;
        ctx.db.create('ticket_event', { ticket_id: id, kind: 'resolved', note, actor_id: t.assignee_id });
        return { status: 200, body: updated };
      }
  reopen_ticket:
    method: POST
    path: /tickets/{id}/reopen
    description: Reopen a resolved ticket. It goes back to open with its assignee, level 0, and a fresh SLA clock from the customer's tier policy. Closed tickets cannot be reopened.
    input:
      reason:
        type: text
        description: Why the ticket is reopened. Stored on the reopened event.
        required: true
        nullable: false
        unique: false
        readonly: false
    handler: |
      (ctx) => {
        const id = ctx.params.id;
        const t = ctx.db.get('ticket', id);
        if (t === null) ctx.fail(404, 'not_found', 'ticket ' + id + ' not found');
        if (t.status === 'closed') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is closed, and closed tickets cannot be reopened. Create a follow-up ticket instead.');
        if (t.status !== 'resolved') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is ' + t.status + '. Only resolved tickets can be reopened.');
        const reason = ctx.body.reason.trim();
        if (reason === '') ctx.fail(400, 'input.invalid', 'Invalid input for reopen_ticket: reason expected a non-blank text, found ""');
        const customer = ctx.db.get('customer', t.customer_id);
        const code = customer.tier + '_' + t.priority;
        const policy = ctx.db.list('sla_policy', { where: { code } })[0];
        if (!policy) ctx.fail(409, 'no_sla_policy', 'no sla_policy ' + code + ' to restart the SLA clock');
        const now = ctx.now();
        const updated = ctx.db.update('ticket', id, {
          status: 'open', resolved_at: null, escalation_level: 0, escalated_at: null,
          sla_started_at: now, sla_due_at: ctx.time.plus(now, policy.resolution_minutes + 'm'), sla_breached: false,
        });
        ctx.db.create('ticket_event', { ticket_id: id, kind: 'reopened', note: reason, actor_id: null });
        return { status: 200, body: updated };
      }
jobs:
  sla_breach:
    description: Every 15 minutes. Pass 1 applies the tier policy to active tickets created without a due time. Pass 2 flags active tickets whose sla_due_at has passed. Pass 3 escalates breached urgent tickets at level 0 to the level 1 on-call agent, the same rule as escalate_ticket.
    every: 15m
    run: |
      (ctx) => {
        const now = ctx.now();
        const active = ['new', 'open', 'pending', 'escalated'];
        const tierOf = {};
        for (const c of ctx.db.list('customer')) tierOf[c.id] = c.tier;
        const target = {};
        for (const p of ctx.db.list('sla_policy')) target[p.code] = p.resolution_minutes;
        for (const t of ctx.db.list('ticket', { where: { sla_breached: false } })) {
          if (!active.includes(t.status)) continue;
          let due = t.sla_due_at;
          if (due === null || due === undefined) {
            const minutes = target[tierOf[t.customer_id] + '_' + t.priority];
            if (minutes === undefined) continue;
            due = ctx.time.plus(t.sla_started_at, minutes + 'm');
            ctx.db.update('ticket', t.id, { sla_due_at: due });
          }
          if (ctx.time.minutesBetween(due, now) < 0) continue;
          ctx.db.update('ticket', t.id, { sla_breached: true });
          ctx.db.create('ticket_event', { ticket_id: t.id, kind: 'sla_breach', note: 'resolution target ' + due + ' passed', actor_id: null });
        }
        const shift = ctx.db.list('oncall_shift', { where: { level: 1 } })
          .find((s) => ctx.time.minutesBetween(s.starts_at, now) >= 0 && ctx.time.minutesBetween(now, s.ends_at) > 0);
        if (!shift) return;
        for (const t of ctx.db.list('ticket', { where: { priority: 'urgent', sla_breached: true, escalation_level: 0 } })) {
          if (t.status !== 'new' && t.status !== 'open' && t.status !== 'pending') continue;
          ctx.db.update('ticket', t.id, { status: 'escalated', escalation_level: 1, escalated_at: now, assignee_id: shift.agent_id });
          ctx.db.create('ticket_event', { ticket_id: t.id, kind: 'escalated', note: 'auto: SLA breach', actor_id: null });
        }
      }
  escalation_timeout:
    description: Every 15 minutes. An urgent ticket that has sat at level 1 for 60 minutes moves to level 2 and to the level 2 on-call agent. Skipped while no level 2 shift covers now.
    every: 15m
    run: |
      (ctx) => {
        const now = ctx.now();
        const shift = ctx.db.list('oncall_shift', { where: { level: 2 } })
          .find((s) => ctx.time.minutesBetween(s.starts_at, now) >= 0 && ctx.time.minutesBetween(now, s.ends_at) > 0);
        if (!shift) return;
        for (const t of ctx.db.list('ticket', { where: { status: 'escalated', priority: 'urgent', escalation_level: 1 } })) {
          if (t.escalated_at === null || ctx.time.minutesBetween(t.escalated_at, now) < 60) continue;
          ctx.db.update('ticket', t.id, { escalation_level: 2, escalated_at: now, assignee_id: shift.agent_id });
          ctx.db.create('ticket_event', { ticket_id: t.id, kind: 'escalated', note: 'auto: level 1 timeout', actor_id: null });
        }
      }
  auto_close:
    description: Every hour. A ticket resolved at least 72 hours ago is closed.
    every: 1h
    run: |
      (ctx) => {
        const now = ctx.now();
        for (const t of ctx.db.list('ticket', { where: { status: 'resolved' } })) {
          if (t.resolved_at === null || ctx.time.minutesBetween(t.resolved_at, now) < 72 * 60) continue;
          ctx.db.update('ticket', t.id, { status: 'closed' });
          ctx.db.create('ticket_event', { ticket_id: t.id, kind: 'closed', note: 'auto: 72h after resolution', actor_id: null });
        }
      }

    why: The original brief requires inactive assignments to fail atomically at assignment time. Failing only later at start does not meet it.
  - decision: 'ticket.technician_id is readonly: ordinary create and PATCH refuse it, and only the assign_ticket action (and seed) may set it.'
    why: This is the only way to stop plain PATCH, mixed PATCH and create from bypassing the active-technician check, and seed can still hold historical data.
  - decision: Refusals are atomic. A refused create, PATCH or assign writes nothing, so a mixed PATCH {technician_id, priority} leaves priority unchanged, and a refused create makes no row.
    why: The brief requires invalid assignments to fail atomically.
  - decision: assign_ticket is allowed only on queued tickets. Active and closed tickets answer 409 invalid_state. Re-assigning a queued ticket to the same or another active technician succeeds.
    why: This keeps start and close rules and the closed-is-final rule intact, and the hard task only needs reassigning queued tickets.
  - decision: "Error codes: 404 not_found for an unknown ticket, 409 technician_inactive for an inactive technician, 409 invalid_state for a non-queued ticket, and a 4xx (input or unknown technician) for a nonexistent technician. A refused readonly field is the engine's standard 4xx."
    why: This follows the conventions of the existing world and the example world, and tests assert 4xx plus unchanged state.
  - decision: start_ticket keeps its technician_inactive and no_technician checks, and its handler is not changed.
    why: Seed-time historical assignments to inactive Dana still exist, so start must keep guarding them. The preserved start rules are unchanged.
  - decision: New tickets are created unassigned and queued. The documented path for a ticket with a technician is create, then assign, then start.
    why: The brief says valid ticket creation must stay available, while technician_id is readonly on create.
  - decision: The easy task keeps its instruction, grader, solution and decoy, because it only PATCHes priority. The medium and hard tasks keep their instructions, intents and difficulty, and their solutions and decoys use POST /tickets/{id}/assign then start. Exactly three tasks remain.
    why: The brief asks to keep the easy task working, make medium and hard use the public assign action, and keep exactly three discriminating tasks.
  - decision: The seed, fixtures, clock (start 2026-01-05T09:00:00.000Z, tick 0s), page sizes and unrelated fields are untouched. No jobs are added.
    why: This is a repair, not a redesign.
outOfScope:
  - what: Unassigning a technician (setting technician_id to null) or reassigning active or closed tickets
    why: Not requested. assign_ticket is for queued tickets only, so start and close rules stay as they are.
  - what: Creating, editing or deactivating technicians through the API
    why: The technician entity keeps its read-only routes and is not part of the repair.
  - what: Changing the seed rows, fixtures, clock or page sizes

  - what: Changing start_ticket or close_ticket behaviour

  - what: Adding or removing tasks

  - what: Jobs, notifications, audit events and technician workload limits

        if (t.status !== 'queued') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is ' + t.status + '. Only queued tickets can be started.');

        const made = ctx.api('POST', '/tickets', { subject: 'Test: toaster will not heat', customer_name: 'Test Customer', priority: 'normal' });

          const again = ctx.api('POST', '/tickets/' + id + '/start', {});

          const c = ctx.api('POST', '/tickets/' + id + '/close', {});

          const c2 = ctx.api('POST', '/tickets/' + id + '/close', {});
